newsitem.title: CHINA: Explosion rocks park in heart of China capital.
newsitem.headline: Explosion rocks park in heart of China capital.

text.p: An explosion rocked a park just yards (metres) from the heart of government in China's capital, Beijing, on Tuesday but police declined to say whether the blast was caused by a bomb or if there were casualties.
"We are investigating," an official at the police station in the Zhongshan park in central Beijing said of the latest in several explosions reported in China's capital this year.

She declined to say whether anyone was wounded in the blast in the Zhongshan park that lies beside the Forbidden City, former home to China's emperors, and is just across the road from the Great Hall of the People where China's leaders meet.
"We will report the details to the public when we are ready," the police official said.
"I can make no further comment," she said, refusing to say whether the explosion was caused by a bomb.
The official also declined to say whether the explosion, which reportedly occurred on Tuesday afternoon, caused serious damage in the park.
Doctors reached at two nearby hospitals said they had received no casualties from any explosion on Tuesday.
Beijing police have already been placed on high alert in China's capital since a bomb exploded on a bus in a central shopping district on March 7.
China's state-controlled media said no one died but several people were wounded in that attack. Police have offered a reward but made no arrests.
Beijing was rocked by at least one other bombing in March, but no casualties were reported.
City officials have said the bombings in Beijing were not linked to earlier attacks in the restive, mainly Moslem region of Xinjiang.

Nine people were killed and 74 injured when three bus bombings rocked Xinjiang's regional capital, Urumqi, on February 25 in an attack that coincided with final funeral rites in Beijing on that day for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
